clue.text: Carpeting material not staying put

parts.note: rep is a ribbed fabric used for upholstery
roving means wandering about, never settling in one place

explanation.surface: A carpet fabric that keeps shifting around on the floor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Carpeting' looks like floor covering, but here it is the British informal sense of a telling-off, as when an employee is 'called on the carpet'.
explanation.definitionFit: To carpet someone is British slang for to scold them, so carpeting is rebuking.

clue.text: Wine jar I put out when empty

indicators.note: put out suggests the letters are disturbed and laid out in a new order

parts.note: something empty holds nothing, a zero, shown as the ring-shaped letter O

explanation.surface: Someone sets out an empty wine jar for the recycling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put out' rearranges JARI together with O (nothing, from 'empty') to give the Spanish wine.
explanation.definitionFit: Rioja is a red or white Spanish table wine named after its region.

clue.text: Bob is a hotel employee

definitions.meaning: a bob is a short haircut, and this is one style of it, cut straight round at jaw level
a young uniformed attendant who carries bags in a hotel

explanation.walkthrough: 'Bob' reads like a man's name working at a hotel; it is the haircut.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a straight-cut bob hairstyle and a boy servant or bellhop.

clue.text: Inaccurate serve results in defeat

parts.note: a tennis shot landing beyond the lines is called out, so out means inaccurate
to do is to serve or suffice, as in 'that will do'

explanation.surface: A tennis player's wayward serve costs them the match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'serve' looks like the tennis stroke but means 'do', as in 'that will serve/do'.
explanation.definitionFit: To outdo a rival is to surpass and so beat them.

clue.text: One member takes part in strikes

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one is I
MP stands for Member of Parliament
to act is to perform or play a part

explanation.surface: A single union member joins in the industrial action.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strikes' suggests walkouts, but it means blows or collisions.
explanation.definitionFit: Impacts are forceful collisions, the same as hits or blows.

clue.text: Time and place

parts.note: a London borough that is a place and also gives its name to the world's reference time

explanation.walkthrough: Greenwich is a district of south-east London, home of the Royal Observatory and of Greenwich Mean Time.
explanation.definitionFit: The London borough is a place, and Greenwich Mean Time is the standard clock reference.

clue.text: Lover of Bess in musical heading off for wild party

indicators.note: heading off says the first letter of the word is removed

parts.note: Porgy loves Bess in Gershwin's musical Porgy and Bess

explanation.surface: A musical's leading man departs for a riotous celebration.
explanation.definitionFit: An orgy is a wild, unrestrained party or revel.

clue.text: Offenders dismissed on orders

parts.note: in cricket a dismissed batsman is out
laws are rules or commands

explanation.surface: Wrongdoers are sent packing by official decree.
explanation.definitionFit: Outlaws are criminals or fugitives from justice.

clue.text: Planning finally approved — delighted!

indicators.note: finally points to the closing letter of the word planning

parts.note: to ratify is to give formal approval

explanation.surface: A homeowner is thrilled that planning permission has at last been granted.
explanation.definitionFit: Gratified means pleased or satisfied.

clue.text: Cricketer yearns to face spinner

parts.note: to long is to yearn
a top is a toy that spins

explanation.surface: A cricketer is eager to take on the opposition's spin bowler.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spinner' suggests a spin bowler, but it is the toy. A long stop is a fielding position in cricket, directly behind the wicketkeeper.
explanation.definitionFit: A long stop is the cricket fielder placed behind the wicketkeeper, so names a player.

clue.text: Catch in Antwerp on the loose without wife

indicators.note: on the loose means running wild, so the letters break free into a new order
without means lacking, so a letter is taken out

explanation.surface: Police try to capture an escaped prisoner in Antwerp.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' removes W from ANTWERP, leaving ANTERP, which 'on the loose' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: To entrap is to catch by trickery.

clue.text: Plant a bomb that explodes overhead

indicators.note: something that explodes is blown apart, so the letters fly into a new order

parts.note: split as over-head: the head, or first letter, of over is O

explanation.surface: A terrorist plants an airburst device.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plant' reads as a verb (plant a bomb) but is the noun. 'explodes' rearranges ABOMB with O.
explanation.definitionFit: Bamboo is a tall woody grass, so a plant.

clue.text: Pot or tin basin broken

parts.note: a tin is a can

indicators.note: broken means smashed, so the letters of basin are reassembled differently

explanation.surface: A list of kitchen containers, some damaged.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broken' rearranges BASIN into NABIS.
explanation.definitionFit: Pot is a slang word for the drug made from hemp.

clue.text: Kept going — or didn't

definitions.meaning: to have lasted or endured, as in staying the course
short for didn't go, that is remained where one was

explanation.walkthrough: The two senses look opposite: endured to the finish, and remained without leaving.
explanation.definitionFit: Stayed means both lasted the distance and remained in place without leaving.

clue.text: Supplementary course?

parts.note: an extra course looks like a class but is a watercourse that feeds into a larger river

explanation.walkthrough: 'course' suggests study, but a river's course is meant.
explanation.definitionFit: A tributary is a stream adding its water to a larger river.

clue.text: Doctor agonised over second opinions

indicators.note: in a down clue, over places the first piece above the next
to doctor is to tamper with, so the letters are altered

explanation.surface: A doctor frets about patients seeking another view.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctor' looks like the physician in the scene, but it is the anagram signal working on 'agonised'.
explanation.definitionFit: Diagnoses are medical judgements, that is professional opinions on a case.

clue.text: Minimum investment for patrons of the pools

definitions.text: Minimum investment for patrons of the pools

parts.words: Minimum investment for patrons of the pools
parts.note: sounds like the smallest stake on the football pools, but means the scantiest clothing for swimmers

explanation.walkthrough: The football pools are a British betting game on match results; 'investment' is also being clothed (invested).
explanation.definitionFit: A swimsuit is the minimal garment swimmers at a pool wear.

clue.text: I was told off for youthful indiscretions

indicators.note: off suggests the letters go astray and are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone recalls being scolded for the mischief of their youth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'told off' reads as scolded, but 'off' alone rearranges I WAS TOLD.
explanation.definitionFit: Sowing wild oats is the idiom for a young person's reckless behaviour.

clue.text: Spotted divine fruit inside

indicators.note: inside puts the fruit between the two letters

parts.note: DD, Doctor of Divinity, stands for a divine or clergyman
an apple is a fruit

explanation.surface: Someone noticed a clergyman with fruit in hand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spotted' looks like 'saw', but means marked with spots.
explanation.definitionFit: Dappled means mottled with spots or patches of colour.

clue.text: Half the school get zero, unusually, for music

indicators.note: half the word school is its first three letters
unusually means in an odd way, so the letters of zero are mixed up

explanation.surface: Half the pupils score nothing in their music exam.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unusually' rearranges ZERO into ERZO.
explanation.definitionFit: A scherzo is a lively movement in a symphony or sonata.

clue.text: Perhaps Hudson Bay may have come from one of these

definitions.text: Perhaps Hudson Bay may have come from one of these

parts.words: Perhaps Hudson Bay may have come from one of these
parts.note: the explorer's name is a rearrangement of these animals, which also bay

explanation.walkthrough: Hudson Bay is a Canadian sea; here Hudson is a jumble of the answer and 'bay' is the howl dogs give.
explanation.definitionFit: Hounds are hunting dogs, which bay or howl.

clue.text: All the same a soldier has to assume it

definitions.text: a soldier has to assume it
definitions.meaning: a soldier must put on regulation dress

explanation.walkthrough: 'All the same' reads as 'nevertheless', but it means identical throughout.
explanation.definitionFit: Uniform means unvarying, and is also the standard dress of soldiers.

clue.text: Party drink is an unusual hit

parts.note: rum is an old British word for odd or strange
to punch is to hit

explanation.surface: A drink served at a party proves surprisingly popular.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unusual' looks like an anagram signal, but it is the British slang sense of rum, meaning odd.
explanation.definitionFit: Rum punch is a mixed alcoholic drink served from a bowl at gatherings.

clue.text: A disposition of arms

parts.note: sounds like troop deployment, but means a way of placing one's own arms

explanation.walkthrough: 'arms' suggests weapons, but it is the limbs, hands on hips with elbows out.
explanation.definitionFit: Arms akimbo means hands on hips with elbows pointing outwards.

clue.text: A bridal path?

parts.note: plays on a bridle path for horses; this is the church passage a bride walks along

explanation.walkthrough: A bridle path is a British track for riders on horseback.
explanation.definitionFit: The aisle is the passage between pews that a bride walks down.

clue.text: Sailor took up crime, seen in the dock

indicators.note: in a down clue, took up means read upwards

parts.note: AB, able seaman, is a sailor
a sin is a wrongdoing

explanation.surface: A sailor turned to crime and ended up in the dock at court.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the dock' suggests a courtroom, but means a harbour enclosure.
explanation.definitionFit: A basin is an enclosed area of water where ships moor.

clue.text: Fills cracks in the decks with stoppers, say

indicators.note: say signals that a word is spoken, giving a word of like pronunciation

parts.note: corks are bottle stoppers

explanation.surface: A shipwright seals the decks' seams with plugs.
explanation.walkthrough: In non-rhotic British speech the two words are pronounced alike.
explanation.definitionFit: To caulk is to seal seams in a ship's deck with waterproof material.

clue.text: Improperly press one for an answer

indicators.note: improperly means wrongly, so the letters are arranged in an incorrect order

explanation.surface: Pushing the wrong button to reply.
explanation.definitionFit: A response is a reply or answer.

clue.text: US polar explorer — and aviator, by the way

parts.note: taken as written
RD, road, is a way

explanation.surface: A note about an American polar pioneer who was also a pilot, added as an aside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by the way' reads as a throwaway aside; RD (road) is a standard abbreviation for a way.
explanation.definitionFit: Richard Byrd was an American naval aviator who flew over both poles.

clue.text: Wheelwright's representative?

parts.note: a wheelwright is literally a man of spokes, read as one who speaks for others

explanation.walkthrough: A wheelwright makes wooden wheels with spokes.
explanation.definitionFit: A spokesman speaks on behalf of others as their representative.
